Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Park Event Center
October 5, 2020
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly
Work Session to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This
allowed for spacing between chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully streamed
through YouTube. You may view this meeting at https://youtu.be/6We2H1yQix0.

Council members present were: Ed Long, Kevin Davis, Norma Naquin, Matt Webber,
Damon Bivins, James Reid and Ron Waymack. Others present: Mayor Ken Kincade,
City Attorney Ben Hooper, City Paralegal Jessica Looper, City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy
Yocom and HR Director Matthew Hood.

City Attorney Ben Hooper announced he was asked by Council Member Doug Warner to
read a letter on his behalf. See attached for copy of letter read by Ben. Ed Long made
a motion to accept Doug's resignation, second by Matt. Motion passed unanimously by
a Roll Call Vote.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid & Webber)

As Chairman, Ed Long opened his committee meeting with a presentation on Human
Animal Support Services (HASS) presented by Director of Community Services Mike
Wheeler. A copy of the presentation is attached to these minutes. No action by
Committee.

Adoption of the Employee Handbook — HR Director Matthew Hood explained this was
the 4" revision since he has been employed with the City. This has been an interactive
process with employees, supervisors and department heads. Additionally, City Attorney
Ben Hooper and Arkansas Municipal League gave input. The legislation will be a
resolution per Ben‘s suggestion. Motion to place this item on this month's Council
Meeting agenda by Ed Long, second by James Reid. Motion passed unanimously.
Annexation of Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A — Laura Nobles, Public Works Director
explained this is before the Planning Commission now, working out some issues but it is
ready to be annexed in. Motion to place this item on this month's Council Meeting
agenda by Matt Webber second by James Reid. Motion passed unanimously.
Authorization for the Lonoke County Housing Authority to Operate within Cabot City
Limits — City Attorney Ben Hooper explained this is an administrative change by Cabot
Housing Authority. Motion to place this item on this month’s Council Meeting agenda
by James Reid, second by Damon Bivins. Motion passed unanimously.

Municipal Services Community Input - None

Mayor Kincade asked for a 2020 budget amendment for a 27" payroll in 2020 due to
the way the calendar falls every 11 to 12 years and the first payday of 2021 falling on

project was started in 2019 but not completed until 2020 making a 2020 budget

Over the past weeks, many of you have heard through conversations, social media, phone calls,
etc, things concerning my personal life. Things that occurred as far back as 30 years ago have
been brought up and misrepresented to affect me and my campaign to be re-elected to the Cabot
City Council. I have made some decisions throughout my life that have not broken the law, but
understandably, some consider questionable. I will answer for them to the Almighty God in my
time. In any case, these are not issues or topics I believe are worthy of campaign conversation,
yet they persist without concern or care for the adverse effects they have on others, many of
whom do not even reside in Cabot.

The campaign season story in Cabot should not be consumed by conversations about personal
lives and matters. It should be about serious issues and the future of our city. Things like
budgets, roads, economic development, and improving quality of life for our citizens, should
dominate the discussion if we are to best serve and further Cabot’s future. However, this is not
the case in many instances.

Social media comments and remarks have caused serious, some profoundly serious, personal and
professional problems for people I love and care about. My family has been affected the most
by this, It has caused pain and many other problems for all my family. This should not
occur, and I apologize publicly to each of them. Careers and futures other than mine have been
adversely affected, some possibly beyond repair. Lives have been severely disrupted by emails,
phone calls, and text messages, many from fake accounts. Children have been brought into a
discussion they know nothing about or have no interest in. This is unfortunate, and very
disappointing.

Organization of which I am a member or on which I have held leadership and Board of Director
positions have received emails and text messages, again, some from fake accounts, that cause me
and the organizations, dire concern. These organizations rely in part on private donations, and an
obvious concern exists that these emails, and social media remarks, will hurt these organizations
and people’s willingness to contribute to what I believe are very worthy and much needed
causes. Even remarks that question the integrity of my decisions on this council have been
brought into question and those remarks do not go unnoticed outside of Cabot.

When lives, careers, and organizations are damaged for political reasons, it becomes time to
evaluate the necessity of the campaign. I have enjoyed overwhelming support and have no doubt
my bid for re-election would be successful. I sincerely appreciate all those who have supported
me, stood by me, and encouraged me in this campaign and during my time on the city council. |
must, however, consider the cost, not just to me, but to loved ones, organizations, and to the
people of Cabot if this campaign continues. I have no doubt that, even with an election victory,
these attacks would continue and people other than myself will continue to be hurt.

on the city council and am ending my campaign for reelection. I respectfully request that the
